bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Daly Cherry-Evans Salary: Hourly to Annual Conversion

When people search for the **daly cherry evans salary**, they often want to know how a given hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, or weekly pay. While the specific salary of a professional athlete is not published in official award data, the calculation method applies to any hourly rate. This guide explains how to convert an hourly rate to annual gross pay, including casual loading and superannuation, using the latest figures from the Fair Work Commission and the Australian Taxation Office.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The standard formula for annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a full-time week of 38 ordinary hours, as defined by the National Employment Standards. For example, if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross pay is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. It is a starting point for budgeting and comparing job offers.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

If you are a casual employee, your employer must pay a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This loading compensates for entitlements like paid annual leave and sick leave that casuals do not receive. The loading is applied before calculating annual pay.

For example, if the base rate is $26.44 per hour (the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026), the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. Using the formula: $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80 per year. The [the timesheet](/) on this site includes a checkbox to add the 25% casual loading automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes loading; the tool adds it for you.

### Award Rates vs. National Minimum Wage

Many employees are covered by a modern award, which sets minimum pay rates higher than the National Minimum Wage. The Fair Work Commission publishes the Modern Awards Pay Database with classification rates, allowances, and penalty rates. For example, the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award (SCHADS) has specific rates for home care workers, with an initial increase of up to 15% from 1 December 2026, as noted in the pay guides from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

If you are award-free, the National Minimum Wage applies. From 1 July 2026, the minimum is $26.44 per hour for adults, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours, as confirmed by the Fair Work Commission. Casual employees get the 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage: $1004.90 × 2 = $2009.80 per fortnight. For a casual on the same base rate: $33.05 × 38 × 2 = $2511.80 per fortnight.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid by your employer into your super fund. It does not reduce your take-home pay. For the 2026–27 year, the super guarantee rate is 12%, with a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. If your annual gross pay exceeds that cap, super is only paid on the first $270,830.

For example, if your annual gross is $65,306.80 (casual NMW), your employer contributes $65,306.80 × 0.12 = $7,836.82 to your super fund. Your take-home pay is still $65,306.80 before tax. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more details.

### Tax and Medicare

Income tax for 2026–27 uses the resident tax-free threshold: nil tax on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% on $45,001 to $135,000, 37% on $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for low-income earners (using 2025–26 thresholds as 2026–27 reductions were not confirmed).

Using the casual NMW example ($65,306.80 annual gross):
- Tax: $18,200 tax-free, then ($45,000 - $18,200) × 15% = $4,020, then ($65,306.80 - $45,000) × 30% = $6,092.04. Total tax = $10,112.04.
- Medicare levy: 2% of $65,306.80 = $1,306.14 (assuming no reduction).
- Net annual pay = $65,306.80 - $10,112.04 - $1,306.14 = $53,888.62.

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

### The Daly Cherry-Evans Salary in Context

While the **daly cherry evans salary** is not listed in the Fair Work Commission's modern awards or the ABS Average Weekly Earnings data, the same conversion principles apply. If you know the hourly rate for any role—whether it's a professional athlete, a nurse, or a retail assistant—you can estimate annual pay using the formula above. The key is to confirm whether the rate includes casual loading and whether super is paid on top.

For award-covered employees, always check the relevant [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. For award-free employees, the National Minimum Wage order sets the floor. Remember that the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page on this site provides the latest figures.

### Summary

- **Annual gross** = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 (assume 38 hours unless otherwise stated).
- **Casual loading** adds 25% to the base rate.
- **Super** is 12% on top of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base.
- **Tax** uses the 2026–27 resident brackets plus 2% Medicare levy.
- The **daly cherry evans salary** is not publicly available from official sources, but the calculation method works for any hourly rate.

For a quick estimate, use [the timesheet](/) on this site. It handles the math for you, including casual loading and super, and provides a breakdown of tax and Medicare.
